description: Progressive-clue identification game. Each item is a figure (answerKind 'person') or a thing (answerKind 'thing'); clues run vague to specific and are revealed one at a time. Every item carries at least one authoritative citation, same rule as the question bank.

clues: As an infant I was hidden, then drawn out of the water and raised in a household not my own.
In exile I met God in a bush that burned without being consumed.
I was sent back to demand freedom for a people enslaved for generations.
On a mountain I received the Law written by God's own finger.
I led the people forty years through the desert but did not myself enter the promised land.
items.explanation: Moses led Israel out of Egypt and mediated the covenant at Sinai; the Catechism presents him as a foreshadowing of Christ the one Mediator.

clues: I was the youngest of my brothers, out watching the sheep when the prophet came to anoint me.
As a boy I faced a giant with a sling and five smooth stones.
I danced before the Ark of the Covenant as it entered my city.
I sinned gravely, then wrote a psalm of repentance that the Church still prays.
God promised that my throne and my house would endure forever.
items.explanation: David, Israel's great king and psalmist, is the ancestor and type of the Messiah; the Catechism calls him the model of prayer in repentance.

clues: My birth was announced to my father in the Temple, and he was struck silent until he named me.
I leapt in my mother's womb when the Mother of the Lord came to visit.
I lived in the wilderness, clothed in camel's hair, eating locusts and wild honey.
I baptized in the Jordan and told the crowds to prepare the way of the Lord.
Pointing to Him, I said, 'Behold, the Lamb of God.'
items.explanation: John the Baptist is the last of the prophets and the immediate precursor of the Lord, sent to prepare His way.

clues: I was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee when I was called to fish for men.
I walked on water toward the Lord, then began to sink when I doubted.
I confessed Him as the Christ, the Son of the living God.
He gave me a new name and the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
I denied Him three times before the cock crowed, then wept bitterly.
items.explanation: Simon Peter, given his name by Christ, is the rock on which the Church is built and the first among the apostles.

clues: I was a Pharisee, zealous for the Law, and I held the coats of those who stoned the first martyr.
On a road, a light from heaven threw me to the ground and a voice asked why I was persecuting Him.
I was blind for three days until a disciple laid hands on me.
I carried the Gospel across the Roman world and wrote letters to the churches I founded.
I called myself the least of the apostles, born out of due time.
items.explanation: Paul, once a persecutor, became the apostle to the Gentiles after his encounter with the risen Christ on the road to Damascus.

clues: My mother wept and prayed for my conversion for many years.
In my youth I chased pleasure and false philosophies, and prayed to be made chaste, but 'not yet.'
In a garden I heard a child's voice chanting 'take up and read.'
The bishop of Milan baptized me, and I became a bishop myself, in North Africa.
I wrote that our hearts are restless until they rest in God.
items.explanation: Augustine of Hippo, Doctor of the Church, recounts his conversion in the Confessions; the Catechism quotes his restless-heart prayer.

clues: I was one of the seven chosen to serve at table so the apostles could devote themselves to preaching.
I was full of grace and power and worked wonders among the people.
Brought before the council, my face was like the face of an angel.
As I was stoned, I saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand.
I died praying that the sin would not be held against my killers.
items.explanation: Stephen, a deacon, is the Church's first martyr; his dying prayer for his persecutors echoes Christ's own.

clues: I entered a Carmelite convent at fifteen and never left it.
I taught a 'little way' of trust and small acts of love rather than great deeds.
I died of tuberculosis at twenty-four, promising to spend my heaven doing good on earth.
My autobiography, Story of a Soul, was read around the world after my death.
Though I never left my cloister, I am a patroness of missionaries, and a Doctor of the Church.
items.explanation: Thérèse of Lisieux, the 'Little Flower,' taught that holiness is reached through confidence and love in ordinary things; the Catechism quotes her definition of prayer.

clues: An angel greeted me as 'full of grace' and told me not to be afraid.
I asked how this could be, since I had no husband, and was told the Holy Spirit would overshadow me.
I answered, 'Let it be done to me according to your word.'
I visited my kinswoman and sang that all generations would call me blessed.
At a wedding I told the servants, 'Do whatever He tells you.'
items.explanation: Mary's free 'yes' at the Annunciation made her the Mother of God; her fiat is the model of faith and obedience.

clues: I was a young deacon at a great council in 325 that met to answer a priest named Arius.
I spent much of my life as bishop of Alexandria, and was exiled five times for my stand.
The saying went that it was 'me against the world' when almost every see wavered.
I insisted the Son is of the same substance as the Father, not a creature.
I wrote that God became man so that man might become God by grace.
items.explanation: Athanasius defended the full divinity of Christ against Arianism, the teaching the Council of Nicaea condemned with the term consubstantial.

clues: I was the son of a great king and a king myself, and God appeared to me in a dream at Gibeon.
Offered anything, I asked not for long life or riches but for an understanding heart.
I settled a dispute between two women by proposing to divide a living child with a sword.
I built the Temple in Jerusalem, a house for the name of the Lord.
My later years were marked by foreign wives and the idolatry they drew me into.
items.explanation: Solomon, David's son, asked God for wisdom to govern and built the first Temple; his fall warns that wisdom is kept only by fidelity.

clues: The Lord had driven seven demons out of me.
I stood by the cross when most of the apostles had fled.
I came to the tomb while it was still dark and found the stone rolled away.
I mistook the risen Lord for the gardener until He spoke my name.
He sent me to announce the Resurrection to the apostles themselves.
items.explanation: Mary Magdalene was the first witness of the Resurrection and was sent by Christ to tell the apostles, earning the title 'apostle to the apostles.'

clues: I was instituted at a supper on the night before He died.
He said the bread was His body and the cup His blood, and told them to do this in memory of Him.
He had already promised that whoever eats this bread would live forever.
The Church calls me the source and summit of the whole Christian life.
Under the appearances of bread and wine, Christ is truly, really, and substantially present.
items.explanation: The Eucharist makes present the one sacrifice of Christ and gives His true Body and Blood; it is the source and summit of the Church's life.

clues: John administered a version of me in the Jordan, but mine as a sacrament came later.
The Lord's command was to make disciples of all nations by way of me, in the name of the Trinity.
I am the gateway to the other sacraments and cannot be repeated.
Through me, original sin and all personal sins are forgiven and one is born again of water and the Spirit.
I make a person a member of Christ and of His Church, and mark the soul permanently.
items.explanation: Baptism frees from sin, regenerates as a child of God, and incorporates into the Church; it is the necessary gateway to the sacramental life.

clues: I was built to exact measure from acacia wood and overlaid inside and out with gold.
Two golden cherubim faced each other above my cover, the mercy seat.
I carried the tablets of the Law, a jar of manna, and Aaron's staff that budded.
I went before the people into battle and around the walls of Jericho.
The Fathers see me fulfilled in the Virgin, who carried the Word made flesh.
items.explanation: The Ark held the signs of God's covenant and marked His presence among Israel; Christian tradition sees Mary as the new Ark, bearing Christ Himself.

clues: I am prayed on a string of beads divided into groups of ten.
My central prayer repeats an angel's greeting and a kinswoman's blessing, ending with a plea for prayers at the hour of death.
Each decade is joined to a scene from the life of Christ and His Mother, called a mystery.
There are now four sets of these mysteries: Joyful, Luminous, Sorrowful, and Glorious.
The Church commends me as a compendium of the whole Gospel prayed alongside Mary.
items.explanation: The Rosary meditates on the mysteries of Christ's life through vocal prayer centered on the Hail Mary; the Church holds it up as a summary of the Gospel.

clues: I was an instrument of Roman execution reserved for slaves and rebels.
The Lord told His followers they must take me up daily and follow Him.
On me the one sacrifice that takes away the sin of the world was offered.
St. Paul said I am folly to those perishing but the power of God to those being saved.
The Church venerates me solemnly once a year, on Good Friday.
items.explanation: The Cross is the altar of Christ's redeeming sacrifice; what the world counts as defeat is the power and wisdom of God.
